title: CLAY COUNTY RACCOON ROUNDUP
full_story:
The Clay County Farm Bureau is launching a “Raccoon Roundup” program to combat rising property damage from an increased raccoon population.

The initiative offers a $3 cash reward per raccoon tail for Farm Bureau members during the upcoming Illinois hunting and trapping seasons.

Two collection events will take place at the Farm Bureau office in Louisville from 6:00 to 7:00 PM tonight and again on Thursday, January 14th  from 6:00 to 7:00 PM.

Participants are limited to 33 tails per collection date and must present a valid DNR hunting or trapping license.  All harvests must strictly follow state regulations.

The Wayne County Farm Bureau is also having a Raccoon Round-ups on November 24th from 6 to 7 pm.  Then on December 8th from 6 to 7 pm and on January 19th from 6 to 7 pm.

title: IUKA FIRES
full_story:
A parked pickup truck was destroyed by fire late Tuesday afternoon in rural Iuka.

The truck was parked on the Barney Sullivan property on Foster Lane.  Residents inside the home say the vehicle had been sitting for about half an hour when they heard an explosion and looked outside to see the engine compartment in flames.

No nearby buildings were threatened by the blaze.  Officials say the cause of the fire has not been determined.

Also on Tuesday afternoon an out-of-control trash fire damaged two vehicles and burned an acre of grass in rural Iuka.

The fire broke out at the Steven Linny home at 501 Johnson Road.  When Kell Firemen arrived on the scene, flames were spreading toward the house, though crews managed to knock the fire down before it reached the home.

Iuka Firemen provided mutual aid at the scene, while Salem crews stood by at the Kell Fire Station to cover any additional calls.

title: NITE PATROL RESULTS
full_story:
Troop Nine Commander Captain Bruce Waggoner announced the results of Nighttime Enforcement Patrols conducted across Effingham, Fayette, Hamilton, Marion, Wabash, And White Counties.

Officers focused on detecting impaired drivers and seatbelt violations between 9 pm and 6 am.

State police issued 53 total citations and arrests.  Which included 5 DUI citations, 21 other alcohol or drug charges, and 56 speeding violations.  Troopers also issued 152 written warnings.

Officials note that over half of all fatal crashes in Illinois occur at night.  And alcohol or drugs are a factor in more than 47% of those fatal accidents.

The special patrol project was funded through the Illinois Department Of Transportation.

title: FREEDOM CAUCUS STATEMENT
full_story:
Campaign season is over, and now it’s time to get back to business in Springfield.  As lawmakers head to veto session next week, the Illinois Freedom Caucus is urging the Governor and the majority party to follow through on their campaign promises to family farmers by passing the Family Farm Preservation Act (HB4736).

The Illinois Freedom Caucus is issuing the following statement:

“This legislation is crucial to saving the future of agriculture and family farms in our state.  Raising the estate tax threshold and adjusting future amounts to inflation are simple common-sense ideas, yet they are also monumental reforms for Illinois’ agriculture community.

The Illinois Farm Bureau has made this estate tax reform their priority for several legislative sessions, gaining increased bipartisan support every year.  The votes are there, and Governor Pritzker himself stated he supports the reform during his 2026 campaign.

When there are rare opportunities such as this to come together on a common sense, pro-taxpayer reform, we should not waste any more time.

title: RUDOLF ASSIGNED
full_story:
Justice David K. Overstreet and the Illinois Supreme Court announced the assignment of Twentieth Judicial Circuit Court Judge Heinz M. Rudolf to the Fifth District Appellate Court.

Judge Rudolf is being assigned to fill the vacancy created by the election of Judge Amy Sholar to the Fifth District Appellate Court where she will fill the late Justice Thomas Welch’s seat.  The assignment of Judge Rudolf is effective December 7th and will continue until further order of the Court.

Judge Rudolf was first appointed to the judiciary in 2006 as an Associate Judge in the Twentieth Judicial Circuit and was reappointed in 2011 and 2015.  He was elected in 2018 as an at-large Circuit Judge where he presides over major civil cases.  Prior to joining the bench, Judge Rudolf worked as an associate for the law firm Becker, Paulson, Hoerner and Thompson, P.C., concentrating on civil defense litigation.  He also served as an Assistant Public Defender and Assistant State’s Attorney in St. Clair County and was an elected member of the St. Clair County Board from 2002 to 2006.

Judge Rudolf has served as a member of the Illinois Judicial Conference Committee on Education and was appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court to serve on the Illinois Judicial College Strategic Planning Committee.  His honors include the Illinois Judges Association’s Presidential Service Award in 2023, the Richard A. Hudlin Award in 2025, which is presented to an attorney who best reflects a commitment to service and charity in St. Clair County, and the Bar Association of Metropolitan St. Louis’ Justice Award in 2026.

Judge Rudolf earned a bachelor’s degree and a Ph.D. in Public Policy Analysis and Administration from Saint Louis University, as well as his Juris Doctor and a Master of Arts in Public Administration through a joint degree program from the Saint Louis University School of Law and Graduate School.

The Fifth Appellate District hears cases from across 48 counties in southern Illinois, including: Clay, Effingham, Fayette, Jasper, Jefferson, Marion, Richland, and Wayne.

title: OPENING SEASON
full_story:
Deer hunters preparing for the open firearm season next weekend will enjoy a spate of pleasant, dry weather before conditions are expected to take a turn for the worse.

“It’s going to be constantly raining,” Freese-Notis Weather Meteorologist Paul Otto said on the RFD Radio Network.  “There’s going to be no avoiding it.  The only direction it’s not going to come from is the east.”

Otto said temperatures are expected to be below normal for the weekend of November 20th through 22nd, but only by roughly 5 degrees.

“Once the system at the start of hunting season moves through, then it allows not one but two batches of cold air to come down straight from polar regions,” he said.  “So, if you have a Thanksgiving Day football game that you play with your family, you could have some snow.”

Temperatures for Thanksgiving Day will reach lows in the teens or 20s.  Otto said it’s possible there will be a rain-snow split along I-64, with rain to the south and snow to the north of the east-west highway.

“As we go into the time when people want to travel at the last second to get to Thanksgiving dinner, or head home, it may potentially be snowy.  This is one of those systems that’s coming from the Pacific Jet Stream, and it will tap into moisture from the western Gulf of Mexico as it nears,” he said.

A true El Nino pattern is expected to set up this winter, Otto added, causing temperatures to continue to seesaw.

“You’ll continue to get batches of heavy rain, but it’s mainly going to be confined to our western areas of the state along the Mississippi River,” he said.  “Cold air is still going to come in, like we’re seeing over Thanksgiving week, and therefore is setting up the picture that we will have some snowstorms.”

Otto expects areas from Quincy down to St. Louis as “being the prime location to possibly see a couple of events that produce heavy snow over the winter.”

title: CARLYLE LAKE SEEKING INTERNS
full_story:
The US Army Corps of Engineers Carlyle Lake Project is gearing up to hire interns for the 2027 summer recreation season.

Officials are hosting an Internship Open House at the Carlyle Lake Visitor Center on Friday, November 27th, at 11 am.  The event will cover job expectations, application steps, and the differences between the Pathways Internship and Student Conservation Association programs.  Current staff will also be on hand to answer questions and talk about their work.

Summer interns help visitors, lead interpretive programs, maintain recreation areas, and assist with environmental projects.

Applicants must be at least 18 years old by the start date, hold a high school diploma or G-E-D by May 31st, 2027, and be enrolled or accepted into a qualifying college, university, or technical school.  Candidates also need at least a 2.0 GPA and must be available to work a full-time, 40-hour schedule that includes weekends and holidays.

For more information, contact the Carlyle Lake Project Office at (618) 594-2484, ext. 3, or email [email protected].

title: LAKE LAND FAST TRACK EVENT
full_story:
Lake Land College is hosting two registration events to help prospective students through the enrollment process for the Spring 2027 semester.  The events, called Fast Track to Spring, will offer one-on-one walkthroughs of the onboarding process.

The Fast Track to Spring events are scheduled for Wednesday, November 18th from 2 to 6 pm and Saturday, January 9th from 8 am to 12 pm.  Both events will be held on Lake Land College’s campus, located at 5001 Lake Land Blvd. in Mattoon.

The Fast Track to Spring events will serve as one-stop shops for prospective students to receive personalized support through the application and registration process.  The events are designed for students of all ages and backgrounds, with both new and returning students welcome.  Representatives from several Lake Land College offices, including Recruitment & Enrollment, Admissions & Records, Counseling, Financial Aid, the Career Readiness Center and more, will also be available during the events to answer questions and ensure each student receives the unique support needed.

“Whether you have a question about scholarships, need help selecting classes or need help getting stated, Fast Track to Spring is the perfect event for you,” said Pam Hartke, Associate Dean of Recruitment & Enrollment Management.  “We’ll have a whole team of people here to help you out and make sure you leave the event ready for your next step toward spring.”

Those interested in attending either of the upcoming Fast Track to Spring events can register now on the Lake Land College website at LakeLandCollege.edu/Visit/.  Registration is recommended to ensure Lake Land College staff can provide each student with a personalized experience.  Walk-ins are also welcome.

To learn more about the Lake Land College Fast Track to Spring events, contact Hartke at 217-238-2705 or [email protected].

Lake Land College Spring 2027 classes begin Monday, January 11th.  To learn more or to enroll, visit the Lake Land College website at LakeLandCollege.edu.

title: ISP HOLIDAY ENFORCEMENT
full_story:
With Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year’s right around the corner, state and local police are locking in plans for their annual holiday enforcement campaigns.  Drivers can expect to see a heavy police presence on major highways and local roads.  Illinois State Police Public Information Officer Ryan Wagand says the goal of these extra patrols is to stop dangerous driving habits before they lead to tragedy.

The high-visibility saturation patrols will focus heavily on impaired driving, speeding, and seatbelt violations throughout the upcoming holiday stretch.
